attributes.title: Exploratory Item Response Matrix Factorization: Bridging Psychometrics and Machine Learning
attributes.description: Recent evolution in psychological and educational assessments has challenged traditional exploratory psychometric methods regarding analyzing high-dimensional sparse data and making accurate predictions, while methods from machine learning present potential for addressing relevant issues. This study proposes Exploratory Item Response Matrix Factorization (EIRMF) based on matrix factorization and compares it with Exploratory Multidimensional Item Response Theory (EMIRT) by simulation data and real data. The results show that tuning the number of factors (as a hyperparameter) in EIRMF can be an effective tool for factor retention analyses compared to methods used in EMIRT. EIRMF slightly outperforms EMIRT in most cases regarding prediction accuracy. For parameter and multidimensionality recovery, we propose Select Pairwise Correlation (spCORR) as a new metric to evaluate methods with other existing metrics. The results show that EIRMF and EMIRT produce highly correlated item intercepts and moderately correlated item slopes and factor scores, and using rotation methods (such as Promax) can improve multidimensionality recovery. A higher number of items and samples improves methods’ performance, while higher levels of factors and missingness show adverse effects. Overall, EIRMF can be an alternative to EMIRT in tasks where EMIRT is less effective with bridging psychometrics and machine learning.
